metaDescription: Six corded 3-in-1 leaf vacuums at or under $100, compared on motor amps, airflow claims, bag design and how well each mulches leaves.
expertTake: The WORX Trivac WG509 is the pick for a balanced, proven corded 3-in-1 with sensible airflow figures. The DUMOS is the value choice if you want a big airflow claim and a bag at the lowest cost tier. Anyone with a large wooded lot or damp, heavy leaves should skip corded vacuums altogether.
introParagraphs: A leaf vacuum swaps the nozzle for a suction tube and a collection bag, and a metal or plastic impeller shreds leaves on the way in. At this level they are all plug-in machines that blow, vacuum and mulch.
What separates them is motor current, impeller material, bag design and how honest the airflow numbers look. Prices move, and the $100 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: WORX Trivac WG509 Corded 3-in-1 Leaf Vacuum
products.description:
The Trivac is the tool most buyers think of first when picturing an electric leaf vacuum, and the spec sheet explains why. It claims 350 CFM and 210 MPH, a balanced pairing that moves leaves into the tube without making it a high-pitched jet. Leaves are pulled through an impeller and shredded, so a full bag holds noticeably more than loose leaves would.

Compared with the DUMOS at 500 CFM, it claims less volume, but the figures look more conservative and the brand has a long record of parts support. The mulching impeller is a plastic wear part that can jam on wet or twiggy material, so clear it with the tool unplugged.

Empty the bag often, keep the intake clear and store it dry. It is the choice for a small to mid yard where you want leaves reduced for compost or lawn mulch. In year three, the parts that matter are the bag, the impeller and the cord, all of which are cheap and easy to source for this model, which is a real point in its favor. Storing it indoors on a hook keeps the plastic from becoming brittle in winter cold. Against a cordless machine, the trade is simple: you give up walking freedom and gain a tool that never needs a battery.
products.bestFor: Small and mid yards that want mulched leaves.
pros: Balanced airflow and air speed claims
Mulching reduces leaf volume in the bag
cons: Plastic impeller can jam on wet leaves

products.name: DUMOS Corded 3-in-1 Leaf Vacuum 500 CFM
products.description:
The DUMOS claims 500 CFM and 167 MPH, giving it a higher volume claim than the Trivac. It is a portable corded machine with a collection bag, and the listing emphasizes faster cleanup through volume rather than raw speed.

The tradeoff is brand certainty. You get more claimed airflow for the money, but fewer assurances about impeller materials, parts supply and how the numbers were measured. Against the PULITUO at 530 CFM, the two are close, so the choice often comes down to bag size and listing support.

Use it on dry leaves and keep the bag from overfilling, because a full bag cuts suction. It suits a buyer who wants the biggest claim at the lowest cost tier. A practical habit with any bag-based machine is to empty it when it is about half full, because suction drops as the bag fills and the motor works harder. Dry leaves compact well in the bag after shredding, so you will empty it less often than the size suggests. Keep a spare dust mask handy, since vacuuming dry leaves lifts fine dust and mold spores.
products.bestFor: Dry leaf cleanup at the lowest cost.
pros: High airflow claim for the cost tier
cons: Thin brand history and parts support

products.name: PULITUO Corded 3-in-1 Leaf Vacuum 530 CFM
products.description:
The PULITUO lists the biggest airflow claim in the group at 530 CFM, with 170 MPH air speed. It is a corded 3-in-1 with a bag, built to blow, suck and shred.

Its airflow claim sits above the DUMOS's 500 and the Heywork's 450, but the real-world gap depends on impeller design and nozzle shape that a spec sheet cannot show. The extra volume helps most when you are vacuuming dry leaves in an open lawn.

Expect a loud motor and plan for hearing protection. Check the bag zipper and keep the impeller clear. It is for buyers who want maximum claimed volume. Because the listing does not publish many specifics, ask yourself whether you are comfortable relying on maker claims alone. If you are, the savings are real. If not, step up to the Trivac or a known hardware brand and accept the smaller claimed airflow in return for more certainty.
pros: Highest airflow claim of the corded group

products.name: Heywork Corded 3-in-1 Leaf Vacuum 450 CFM
products.description:
The Heywork claims 450 CFM and 158 MPH, placing it between the Trivac and the DUMOS on volume. It is a corded multi-function tool with an orange body that is easy to spot.

The lower speed claim means it handles dry leaves and clippings well but struggles to lift wet ones. It is similar in concept to the DUMOS, so choose between them on bag size and what the listing includes.

Store it dry and empty the bag after each use. It fits a modest yard. Because this one is cheap to run, it makes a sensible second tool for a workshop or garage floor too, where its blower mode clears sawdust and grit. Expect a loud motor under load and use hearing protection. Roll the cord loosely when storing it, rather than tight around your arm, to avoid kinks.
pros: Corded power with no pack to replace
cons: Lowest air speed claim of the group

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Corded 3-in-1 Handheld 12-Amp
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER offers a handheld 3-in-1 with a 12-amp motor and a 230 MPH claim. It converts from blower to vacuum and includes a mulching function, from a maker whose replacement bags and impellers are easy to find.

The focus is on air speed rather than a headline CFM figure, which suits stuck debris on a deck or driveway more than piles on a lawn.

Choose it if brand and parts availability matter more than the biggest airflow claim. The handheld layout is easy on the arm for short jobs, but a bag hanging at the side gets heavier as it fills, so plan to empty it before it drags on your shoulder. Replacement bags and impellers are the parts most owners eventually buy, and they are widely stocked for this maker. For routine care, wipe the intake and shake out the bag.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 12-Amp Corded 3-in-1 Blower Vacuum
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN also uses a 12-amp motor but claims the highest air speed in the group at up to 260 MPH. It blows, vacuums and mulches from one corded body.

Speed helps lift debris off pavement, but vacuuming depends on volume, which the listing does not state. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER at 230 MPH, it pushes slightly harder.

Keep the cord rated for a 12-amp load. The speed-first design is excellent for blowing leaves out of corners and off hard surfaces, but if you want to vacuum, be realistic about volume. Use the blower mode to bring leaves into a pile, then switch to vacuum with the tube to collect and shred them. That two-step method uses the strengths of each mode.
products.bestFor: Pavement debris and light leaf work.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The BLACK+DECKER and CRAFTSMAN use 12-amp motors, which supply plenty of power for blowing and shredding. Check the cord gauge, since 12 amps over a thin cord overheats and loses power. Check the cord rating on the package, and keep extension runs under fifty feet where possible to limit voltage drop. Plan the whole setup, including the cord, before you buy.

Mulching impellers are either plastic or metal. Plastic is cheaper and can crack on twigs, while metal lasts longer. At this price, expect plastic and avoid feeding it sticks. Metal impellers are rare at this price, so the practical rule is to keep sticks out of the intake and pre-clear branches by hand.

A bag that fills quickly interrupts work. Look for a zipper that opens fully, and empty it before it cuts suction. Look at how the bag attaches, because a bag with a weak clip or zipper is the most common annoyance owners report.

The PULITUO claims 530 CFM and the CRAFTSMAN 260 MPH. Volume matters for pulling leaves into the tube, speed for blowing. If your yard is mostly lawn, favor volume; if it is mostly driveway and deck, favor speed.

Converting from blower to vacuum takes steps and sometimes tools. If you switch often, handle design matters. Make a habit of checking the lock on the tube, since a loose latch while vacuuming can drop the tube and jam the impeller.
A thin extension cord starves a 12-amp motor. Use a heavy-gauge outdoor cord. Wear eye and ear protection, because shredded leaf fragments exit at high speed and the motor is loud.

specDecoder.meaning: Current drawn by a corded motor. More amps allows more power. Match the cord gauge to this number.
specDecoder.watchFor: The BLACK+DECKER and CRAFTSMAN are 12 amps; others do not state it.

specDecoder.meaning: Claimed volume of air. Higher volume pulls more leaves. Treat as a best-case maker figure.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PULITUO claims 530 CFM and the Trivac 350, but methods differ.

specDecoder.meaning: Claimed air speed for lifting debris. Higher numbers help lift debris from pavement.
specDecoder.watchFor: The CRAFTSMAN claims 260 MPH versus the DUMOS at 167.

specDecoder.meaning: How much the impeller shrinks leaf volume. A higher ratio means fewer trips to empty bags.
specDecoder.watchFor: Not stated on most listings in this group.

specDecoder.meaning: Volume of the collection bag. A bigger bag trades weight for fewer stops.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated amps and airflow claims. The CRAFTSMAN and BLACK+DECKER state 12 amps. Others were judged on claims. That comparison matters because a stated 12-amp draw tells you more about real power than a headline CFM number from an unfamiliar maker.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mulching design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at impeller descriptions and bag design. Plastic impellers were noted as a wear point. Plastic impellers were treated as acceptable at this cost tier but as a clear wear point owners should plan for.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claim realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared CFM and MPH claims against plausible motor power. Claims of 530 CFM were treated as best case. We also noted that a claim without a stated measurement point cannot be compared directly across brands, so we ranked within groups.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brand support
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered parts availability. The WORX and BLACK+DECKER scored higher than newer import brands. Where parts availability was unclear, we marked the tool down for ownership even if its airflow claim was strong.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at mode switching and bag handling from the listings. We favored designs where the bag opens fully and the tube latches cleanly, because those are the details owners comment on most.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A mulching impeller and a bag that fills slowly. Shredded leaves break down far faster than whole ones.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WORX Trivac WG509 is the best fit for composting, with the PULITUO the volume alternative.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want cordless freedom or a metal impeller. Cordless 40V vacuums sit above this cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small yard with dry leaves. The DUMOS or Heywork is enough.

maintenance.why: A full bag cuts suction. Empty it before it clogs the tube. Check the bag seams for tears each autumn, since a split bag blows dust back at you.
Wet leaves wrap the impeller. Unplug and clear it before overheating. Store the machine upright and dry, with the tube detached, to avoid warping.
Nicks in a cord are a shock hazard.
Dust blocks cooling slots and heats the motor.

faq.q: Is a corded vacuum strong enough for leaves?
faq.a: For dry leaves on a small to mid yard, yes. Wet leaves clog the impeller. For a quick patio job, a plain blower is simpler, but for composting a vacuum earns its place.
It is how many bags of leaves become one bag of mulch. Most listings do not state it. Wet leaf paste also dries hard inside the housing, so clean it out the same day.

faq.q: Do I need a heavy extension cord?
faq.a: Yes, for 12-amp motors. A thin cord overheats. Expect to see numbers listed as best case, so treat the highest ones with caution.
They clog the impeller. Let leaves dry or use a stronger machine. Cord gauge matters more than most buyers expect, particularly in cold weather when the cable stiffens.
Not across brands. Compare within a brand or use motor amps as a guide.
